revisions.reason: After L50/L51 inspection: the concept image reimposes continuous walls approaching the collar. Remove AI concept sample and strengthen explicit native-deck interval for the remaining five generations.
revisions.previous_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. ONE new concept sheet for the exact Freelancer li_pir_elite, developing the positively received paired obelisk-like hull-side idea with more freedom in its local shape. Keep the native multi-faceted longitudinal BLOCK body, cabin, basic proportions, Art Deco / Empire surface-art vocabulary, two unequal vertically stacked polygonal rear engines and separate transverse aft spoiler. The owner wants variants of THIS ship, not a different fighter architecture.

Reference roles:
1. EXACT immutable native cockpit: shell, size, elongated low capsule proportions, pane shapes and thin frames must match this reference. No stretching, enlarged glazing, replacement canopy or added nose.
2. Actual native li_pir_elite: primary whole-ship geometry, lower block, wing fan lineage, red/ochre/pale fan-painted panels, original side frieze, stern motif, polygonal engine bodies and proportions. These override the concept sample for source identity.
3. L45 is a positively received DIRECTION, not a frozen design. Borrow the two solid raised side masses, recessed middle and native-looking treatment. Do NOT automatically carry its side masses forward to the collar. Their length, onset, rake, height, taper and stern junction MUST follow the individual variant below. Different outline, not only different engraved patterns.
4. Native cargo closed/open: two longitudinal leaves, fore-aft seam, outer long-edge hinges. Keep the hatch/deck visibly lower BETWEEN the raised masses. Leave broad usable central clearance, a real hold with walls and floor, and room for door opening. No new flush roof over the middle. The moving leaves are secondary to the body.
5. Actual wing motion: broad overlapping leaves with a compact forward root and nesting backward along the sides when stowed. Preserve the native leaf count unless the variant EXPLICITLY requests the authorized two-leaf experiment. Changed leaf counts are a concept proposal, not a claim of original mechanics.

The two obelisk-like masses are SOLID extensions of the original hull flanks, tapering inward toward their tops, composed of deliberate flat facets. They are not thin skeletal rails, freestanding stone towers or added rod frames. Preserve the original lower body silhouette. A clear interval of native deck may separate their forward ends from the collar: this is now encouraged. Collar treatment is specified per variant; its external flange may have real local notches, but the cabin shell/glass is always untouched. The native crosswise aft spoiler should rise slightly above the highest side mass, with a developed outline as specified below. Two original engines remain VERTICALLY stacked underneath: do not invent a lateral pair or replace them with big rectangular radiator boxes.

Surface style must look like original li_pir_elite: worn native red and ochre skin, pale radial fan/frieze artwork and restrained shallow relief derived from it, dark recessed fields, native blue-grey glass. Modest fluting and shaped borders may emphasize structural faces. No massive gold picture-frame overlays, random greebles, rivet geometry, pipes, spikes, cathedral towers or unrelated Empire furniture. Pirate character comes from the source materials and a few integrated repair fields, not a new palette. Think a few designed nuances on the source hull, not a replacement ship.

Presentation: landscape production concept sheet on quiet pale-grey background, crisp native-scale shapes and moderate detail. One LARGE front-side three-quarter view from slightly above, nose to lower LEFT; see both raised sides, the recessed central deck, the original cabin and raised spoiler clearly. Supporting small FRONT, SIDE, TOP and CARGO OPEN views of precisely the SAME ship. Arrange small views with enough space, main view dominates. Show doors raised in CARGO OPEN without moving the fixed side masses; this is a concept diagram, not an exploded assembly. Keep engine stacking and number of wing leaves consistent across all views. Top may be nose UP or LEFT as layout permits. Labels only the concept ID and FRONT / SIDE / TOP / CARGO OPEN. No arrows or blue/green annotations.

SPECIFIC VARIANT, overrides the sample's pylon/collar connection:
In TOP the paired raised side masses diverge subtly toward the stern: their forward ends are closer to the centerline, while their aft crowns sit over the wider original body shoulders. Stay WITHIN the native hull footprint; do not enlarge the lower ship. Begin the masses after the original collar, with a low deck gap. The upper central well therefore widens a little aft while the two longitudinal cargo leaves remain straight and smaller than the whole well. Each side mass still tapers inward in FRONT cross-section. The side tops are low, broad and nearly level, not steep towers. Rear spoiler follows the source span with two clipped outward end facets and a higher short central cornice. Retain source collar complete. Emphasize changing top-view spacing of the two solid upper volumes, not merely a decorative trapezoid.
WING COUNT for L52: 3 full moving leaves on EACH side. Label sheet L52.
